data.name: Hero Generations: ReGen
data.detailed_description:
Elogiado como sendo um "descendente do jogo Civilization de Sid Meier's, Passage de Jason Rohrer's e The Legend of Zelda", Hero Generations é um jogo Roguelike/4X Strategy onde cada jogada custa um ano de vida ao herói.

Explora, encontra a tua cara-metade, constrói uma casa e tem um filho antes de morreres, para manteres o teu legado. Hero Generations é simples, mas mesmo assim profundo: 4X Strategy ao nível individual. Cada jogada um é escolha consciente, sem teres de te preocupar com todo o pequeno detalhe

ESPERANÇA DE VIDA LIMITADA E MORTE PERMANENTE
Cada jogada consome um ano de vida do herói. Pensa bem como vais gastar o tempo de vida do herói. Explora o mundo para ganhares fama e fortuna, mas certifica-te que encontras uma companheira antes que seja tarde de mais!

GERAÇÕES, ACASALAR E TER FILHOS
Encontra a tua cara-metade, começa uma família e tem um filho. Controla essa criança no mesmo mundo em que nasceu! A escolha da(o) companheira(o) é a chave, pois a criança herda as características dos pais, tornando-a mais poderosa e preparada para a vida.

6 CAMINHOS ESTRATÉGICO
Guia o teu herói para a excelência Explorando o mundo, em busca de Força, Amor, Riqueza, Fama e Construindo edifícios.

SISTEMA DE CRIAÇÃO DE CIDADES
Constroi qualquer um dos 19 edifícios próximos das cidades que se mantiveram durante o teu legado. Dá às gerações futuras recursos uteis, habilidades poderosas e atrais melhores companheiras(os).

MUNDO EXPANSIVO
Cada mundo é gerado de forma aleatória com cidades, florestas, ruínas antigas, heróis e muito mais. Descobre os 6 tipos distintos de biomas (Floresta, Deserto, Prados, Ilhas, Favelas e Vulcões) num mapa do mundo gigante.

SIGNIFICADO
Uma experiência surpreendente e que convida à reflexão sobre temas como a morte, o legado, família, amor entre outros.
Um maravilhoso estilo artístico desenhado à mão.

OUTRAS FUNCIONALIDADES
- Árvore tecnológica de construção e plantas de edifício
- Muitos objectos, caracteristicas/habilidades, edifícios, missões, incluindo o fim do mundo em eventos gerados de forma aleatória e um super-monstro
- Pontuações online e conquistas
- Jogo bastante fluido, com efeitos de luz e partículas, assim como animações criadas através do motor de jogos Unity

reviews.review:
Hero Generations: ReGen is an imaginative strategy adventure that combines roguelike progression, exploration, and generational storytelling into a surprisingly thoughtful experience. Developed and published by Heart Shaped Games LLC, the game introduces a fascinating concept where every movement represents one year of the protagonist's life. Rather than concentrating on a single hero's accomplishments, players must establish a lasting family legacy through successive generations. This unusual approach transforms ordinary decisions into meaningful strategic considerations, creating an experience where time becomes the most valuable resource.

The central gameplay mechanic revolves around balancing exploration with the unavoidable passage of time. Every step brings the hero closer to death, forcing players to carefully evaluate their priorities. Discovering treasure, fighting enemies, collecting resources, and visiting distant settlements can provide valuable rewards, but excessive exploration may leave insufficient time to establish a family. This creates an interesting tension between personal ambition and long-term survival. The system encourages deliberate planning, although its restrictive nature can occasionally make experimentation feel unnecessarily punishing.

One of the game's most distinctive features is its generational progression system. Players must find a suitable partner, produce an heir, and eventually continue their adventure through the next generation. Children inherit traits and special abilities from their parents, potentially becoming more capable than their predecessors. This creates an engaging cycle of gradual improvement, where each hero contributes something to the family's future. Watching descendants benefit from previous accomplishments provides a satisfying sense of continuity. However, repeatedly searching for partners can become tedious, particularly when unfavorable circumstances interfere with carefully planned objectives.

Exploration unfolds across a procedurally generated fantasy world featuring towns, ancient ruins, hostile creatures, and varied environments. Six distinct biomes, including forests, deserts, meadows, islands, swamps, and volcanic regions, provide opportunities for discovery. The interconnected overworld encourages players to investigate unfamiliar territories while carefully managing their limited lifespan. Procedural generation adds replayability, ensuring that different adventures present changing circumstances. Nevertheless, the environments occasionally lack sufficient mechanical variety, and repeated journeys can expose the simplicity of certain activities.

Strategic flexibility contributes significantly to the game's appeal. Players can pursue six different approaches to success through Strength, Love, Exploration, Wealth, Fame, and Building. These alternatives encourage experimentation with different priorities and development strategies. Some heroes may concentrate on accumulating resources, while others focus on discovering new territories or improving settlements. The freedom to approach progression through multiple objectives helps distinguish the experience from traditional role-playing adventures. However, certain strategies feel more rewarding than others, and the underlying mechanics may appear relatively shallow to players accustomed to complex grand strategy games.

Settlement development introduces another important dimension through a construction system featuring 19 different building types. Structures established near towns can provide resources, unlock abilities, and create advantages for future generations. Experimenting with building combinations can also produce specialized settlements, including castles, fortresses, and dark cathedrals. These persistent improvements reinforce the central theme of leaving something valuable behind. The accompanying technology tree expands progression possibilities, although the construction mechanics remain relatively accessible rather than overwhelmingly complicated.

Combat provides additional challenges through encounters with enemies scattered across the world. Character abilities, equipment, and preparation influence survival, making unnecessary confrontations potentially dangerous. Because death can interrupt generational progress, players must consider whether fighting is worth the risk. Unfortunately, combat lacks the tactical sophistication of more dedicated strategy titles. Encounters can become predictable, and the limited mechanical complexity may disappoint players seeking elaborate battles. Nevertheless, combat serves its purpose by introducing meaningful obstacles that complement the broader survival mechanics.

Visually, the game features an appealing hand-drawn fantasy style supported by colorful environments, recognizable characters, and improved animations. As a remake of the original Hero Generations, ReGen introduces higher-resolution graphics, a seamless overworld, additional quests, expanded content, and technical improvements through the Unity engine. The presentation is charming rather than visually spectacular, but its simplicity complements the accessible gameplay. The interface generally communicates essential information effectively, although understanding the relationships between different systems requires some initial patience.

The game also explores surprisingly meaningful themes involving mortality, family, sacrifice, and personal legacy. Each protagonist eventually dies, but their accomplishments can influence descendants and gradually transform the surrounding world. This creates an unusual emotional connection to progression, where success depends less on individual greatness and more on what remains for future generations. Additional features such as generational events, a final boss, achievements, leaderboards, and a digital art book provide supplementary value. However, repeated playthroughs may become predictable as the fundamental cycle of exploration, reproduction, and inheritance begins to feel familiar.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Hero Generations: ReGen is officially classified as Unsupported. Although its turn-based mechanics and modest graphical requirements might appear suitable for handheld gaming, reliable operation on Steam Deck is not guaranteed. Players intending to experience the game primarily on Valve's portable system should consider this limitation.

Overall, Hero Generations: ReGen succeeds through creativity, thoughtful mechanics, and an unconventional interpretation of character progression. Its combination of aging, inheritance, exploration, and settlement development offers a refreshing alternative to conventional strategy adventures. While repetitive objectives, simplistic combat, and occasionally frustrating time restrictions prevent it from achieving greater depth, its distinctive premise remains compelling. Players who appreciate experimental independent games and strategic experiences built around meaningful consequences will find considerable value in its unusual approach to survival and legacy.

Rating: 7/10
